action: No action needed; for awareness. Affected customers are being notified by email; treat unexpected emails that use your name with caution.
date_note: NHK (published 12 November, 20:44 JST) reports USMH announced the unauthorized access that day; Security NEXT, which first reported it here, was published on 20 November.
exec: A third-party compromise of a retailer's shopping app system may have leaked customer names and email addresses of 64,003 accounts.
plain: A third party compromised the system of the supermarket group's Scan&Go ignica app; names and email addresses of 64,003 accounts may have leaked.

sources.name: NHK (lead paragraph only; article body gated)

summary: According to Security NEXT, United Super Markets Holdings (USMH) found that the system of its smartphone shopping app Scan&Go ignica was compromised by a third party. A file with some customers' names and email addresses, entered at registration, was found on the system; 64,003 accounts of about 2.4 million registered may have leaked. The company says no misuse or secondary harm has been confirmed.
title: USMH: Scan&Go ignica shopping app system compromised, 64,003 accounts may have leaked

validation.note: Security NEXT and NHK each report USMH's announcement of unauthorized access and about 64,000 records (names, email addresses). NHK read only to its lead paragraph; USMH's own notice not read.

review.note: Compared title, 64,003 of about 2.4M accounts, names and emails, no misuse confirmed, email notice against Security NEXT; NHK lead (12 Nov, about 64,000 records) confirms announcement date
